notes.16: Candidates found this question difficult. More than twice as many candidates chose incorrect option A rather than key C. Option A was derived by deducting $4320 (interest on capital) and $18 000 (salary) from $140 000 (profit) and taking the partner’s share of 20 per cent. However, these two elements are allocations of profit in themselves so needed to be added to the residual profit share to derive the total profit. Thus $23 536 + $4 320 + $18 000 = $42 856 = key C. Candidates therefore needed to be alert to realise that they were being asked to calculate the share of total profit rather than just the residual profit.

notes.general_comments:
Of the candidates who sat this examination, 60 per cent achieved a score of 15 or more correct answers.
The mean score was 16 marks. Questions 4, 9, 11, 14, and 18 proved straightforward with 70 per cent or
more of candidates identifying the correct key. Only one question proved challenging and this has been
considered below.
